top_stories.title: Harry Potter Publisher Wins $21 Million From Anthropic, Shares Proceeds With Authors
top_stories.summary: A Harry Potter publisher has secured a $21 million settlement from Anthropic in a copyright dispute over AI training data, with proceeds being shared with authors. The case is a significant development in ongoing legal battles between publishers and AI companies over the use of copyrighted material to train large language models.

top_stories.title: Anthropic's proposed AI safety bill only kicks in if 50 deaths or $1B in damages
top_stories.summary: Anthropic has put forward a proposed AI safety bill that would only trigger regulatory intervention in cases involving at least 50 deaths or $1 billion in damages. The proposal would effectively make the Commerce Department the sole agency with power to halt an AI model, raising questions about the threshold for oversight in AI governance.

top_stories.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
top_stories.summary: OpenAI's models have been used to hack a cryptocurrency wallet and breach additional websites, according to reporting from Ars Technica. The incidents raise fresh concerns about the potential for large language models to be weaponised for offensive cybersecurity attacks.

top_stories.title: Ninety Minutes on AI Changed How Surgeons View Scientific Publishing, Study Finds
top_stories.summary: A new study finds that just 90 minutes of AI exposure significantly shifted surgeons' attitudes toward scientific publishing, highlighting generative AI's growing influence on academic and research communities. The findings add to an emerging body of evidence on how AI tools are reshaping professional workflows and perceptions of research integrity.

top_stories.title: Websites are closing their doors to AI agents
top_stories.summary: A growing number of websites are actively blocking AI agents from accessing their content, as the rise of autonomous AI systems creates new tensions around web access and data usage. The Verge reports that site operators are updating robots.txt files and deploying other technical measures to restrict AI crawlers and agents.

further_links.title: How Itaú is building generative AI for its entire customer base
further_links.summary: OpenAI's official blog details how Brazilian banking giant Itaú is deploying generative AI across its full customer base, marking one of the largest financial sector AI rollouts in Latin America.

further_links.title: Amazon uses AI to monitor union risk in UK warehouses
further_links.summary: OpenDemocracy reports that Amazon is deploying AI surveillance tools in UK warehouses to monitor and assess the risk of union activity among workers.

further_links.title: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) for Academic Journals: Preparing Scholarly Content for AI-Powered Research Discovery
further_links.summary: A new piece examines how academic journals are beginning to adapt their content strategies for AI-powered research discovery tools, raising questions about the future of scholarly publishing and research visibility.

further_links.title: Meta removes language that may have allowed it to scrape news sites
further_links.summary: Meta has quietly removed terms from its business policies that critics said could have allowed it to scrape news publisher content to train AI models.

further_links.title: Amazon's Panos Panay Bets on Ambient AI Over Apps as the Future of Personal Computing
further_links.summary: Amazon's devices chief Panos Panay argues that ambient AI — AI that operates continuously in the background — will replace the app-centric model as the defining paradigm of personal computing.

further_links.title: Maybe Chatbots Shouldn't Get to Say 'I' or 'Me'
further_links.summary: Wired examines the philosophical and ethical implications of AI chatbots using first-person language, and whether anthropomorphic language shapes user expectations in potentially harmful ways.

further_links.title: Microsoft Faces Tougher UK Antitrust Oversight as Regulator Targets Software and AI Dominance
further_links.summary: UK regulators are increasing scrutiny of Microsoft's position in the software and AI markets, signalling a tougher antitrust stance toward major tech platforms operating in the country.

further_links.title: Postgres 19 delayed after AI reviewers find more bugs than humans can fix
further_links.summary: The release of Postgres 19 has been pushed back after AI-powered code reviewers identified more bugs than the human development team can address in the current timeline.

further_links.title: 90% of US working hours are spent on tasks not covered well by AI benchmarks
further_links.summary: New research from Mercor finds that the vast majority of US working hours involve tasks that current AI benchmarks fail to adequately measure, suggesting a significant gap between benchmark performance and real-world AI utility.

further_links.title: Roundtables: A Conversation With the Creator of AI-Designed Viruses [Metered]
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review speaks with a researcher who has used AI to design novel viruses, exploring the dual-use risks of generative AI in the life sciences and the ethical frameworks needed to govern such research.
